# Defensive Review

## System Overview
- AttackMap reviewed a web/service-facing codebase with 3 inferred entry points across 1 scanned files.
- Raw inferred entry points: 3
- Observed runtime/public surfaces: 3
- Protocol/lexicon-derived surfaces (inferred): 0
- Internal-only surfaces: 0
- Test/example/mocked surfaces (down-weighted): 0
- Languages: javascript
- Datastores: mysql
- External dependencies observed: 0
- Identified assets: 1 | controls observed: 0 | control absences: 6

## Notable Observations
- **[CRITICAL]** Public route reaches User credentials at rest without observed auth _(confidence=medium, kind=sensitive_asset_reachability)_
  - User credentials at rest (criticality=critical) lives in modules that are reachable from 3 public route(s) with no observed authentication signals on the surface. This means an unauthenticated attacker can directly invoke handlers in the same module as a high-value asset without traversing an explicit auth boundary.
  - _Suggested action:_ Add an explicit authentication guard at the route boundary or relocate the handler out of the asset's module so the trust boundary is visible in code.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1190` Exploit Public-Facing Application, `T1041` Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
  - _Evidence:_ `POST /import (app.js:8) — exposure=public, auth_signals=none`; `POST /signup (app.js:13) — exposure=public, auth_signals=none`; `GET /orders (app.js:19) — exposure=public, auth_signals=none`
- **[HIGH]** User credentials at rest has gaps in expected controls: authentication \(absent\), encryption\_at\_rest \(absent\), audit\_logging \(absent\) _(confidence=medium, kind=control_strength_mismatch)_
  - User credentials at rest is criticality=critical, which would normally warrant strong controls of kind: authentication, encryption_at_rest, audit_logging. The scan observed gaps in: authentication (absent), encryption_at_rest (absent), audit_logging (absent). These may exist but are not detectable from code signals — either way, the absence in static evidence is itself worth confirming.
  - _Suggested action:_ Either add the missing controls or annotate the code path where they live so subsequent scans can pick them up.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1110` Brute Force, `T1552` Unsecured Credentials
  - _Evidence:_ `asset:asset:credentials → expected:authentication`; `asset:asset:credentials → expected:encryption_at_rest`; `asset:asset:credentials → expected:audit_logging`
- **[HIGH]** Chain \`Object-level authorization bypass \(BOLA/IDOR\)\` reaches a data store with no authentication, input\_validation, rate\_limiting signals along the way _(confidence=medium, kind=defense_gap_in_chain)_
  - The inferred path `Object-level authorization bypass (BOLA/IDOR)` (Horizontal privilege escalation — attackers modify other users' objects by changing an id in the request.) terminates at a data store but the codebase has no observable signals for authentication, input_validation, rate_limiting along this path. That means a request landing on the entry surface can be carried through to the sink without any of those defenses being applied — at least, none that the heuristic scanner can see.
  - _Suggested action:_ Add explicit middleware for authentication, input_validation, rate_limiting on the entry route, or document where these controls live so they show up to static analysis.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1190` Exploit Public-Facing Application, `T1212` Exploitation for Credential Access
  - _Evidence:_ ``path step: Entry: An attacker calls POST /import in app.js, which takes a resource id (`id`)``; `path step: Weak point: No ownership or authorization check is visible in the handler — the resource id from the request is trusted directly`; ``path step: Propagation: The attacker enumerates or substitutes `id` values; datastore hint in the route's file, so the query returns another principal's record``
- **[MEDIUM]** Sensitive assets present, no audit-logging signals detected _(confidence=medium, kind=audit_gap)_
  - 1 sensitive asset(s) were identified — User credentials at rest — but no audit-logging signals were detected anywhere in the scan. Without audit trails for sensitive-asset access, post-incident forensics and detection-engineering are constrained.
  - _Suggested action:_ Add structured audit logging at handlers that touch sensitive assets; include actor, action, asset id, and outcome.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1685` Disable or Modify Tools
  - _Evidence:_ `asset:asset:credentials (critical)`

## ATT&CK Techniques Mapped
- `T1041` **Exfiltration Over C2 Channel** — _Exfiltration_
- `T1078` **Valid Accounts** — _Stealth / Persistence / Privilege Escalation / Initial Access_
- `T1110` **Brute Force** — _Credential Access_
- `T1190` **Exploit Public-Facing Application** — _Initial Access_
- `T1195.001` **Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools** — _Initial Access_
- `T1212` **Exploitation for Credential Access** — _Credential Access_
- `T1505.003` **Server Software Component: Web Shell** — _Persistence_
- `T1552` **Unsecured Credentials** — _Credential Access_
- `T1685` **Disable or Modify Tools** — _Defense Impairment_

## Detection Opportunities
- **Alert on unauthenticated access to sensitive-asset routes** _(signal=log)_
  - _Why:_ A static-analysis gap on auth at the surface is also a runtime detection opportunity: any 2xx response for these routes from a request lacking a valid session/JWT is high signal.
  - _Suggested rule:_ On the access log: alert when status_code IN (200,201,204) AND route IN (`/import`, `/signup`, `/orders`) AND request_headers.authorization IS NULL AND session_cookie IS NULL. Tighten with a low-volume baseline — this should normally be zero.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1190`, `T1041`
- **Add config-drift detection for missing controls on critical assets** _(signal=config_audit)_
  - _Why:_ When critical assets exist but expected controls aren't observable, drift detection on the deployed configuration (WAF rules, IAM policies, encryption-at-rest flags) gives ongoing visibility even before code-level fixes land.
  - _Suggested rule:_ Add a daily IaC/config audit step: assert that the modules holding critical assets have (a) a WAF/auth policy attached, (b) database encryption-at-rest enabled, (c) audit-log subscriptions configured. Page when any assertion regresses.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1110`, `T1552`
- **Add request-tracing to confirm controls actually run on this chain** _(signal=trace)_
  - _Why:_ Static analysis can't tell whether a control is invoked at runtime. Trace spans on the entry and sink confirm whether intermediate auth/validation/rate-limit middleware actually executed.
  - _Suggested rule:_ Instrument the chain's entry handler and its sink (DB call) with OpenTelemetry spans. Alert when a sink span's parent trace lacks a span tagged `middleware=auth` or `middleware=ratelimit`. This catches code paths that bypass middleware via direct invocation.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1190`, `T1212`
- **Establish baseline audit logs on sensitive-asset access** _(signal=log)_
  - _Why:_ Detection is only as good as the telemetry available. The lack of audit-logging signals in code is a precondition: there is nothing for a SIEM to reason over.
  - _Suggested rule:_ Emit a structured audit record `{actor, action, asset_id, outcome, request_id}` from every handler that touches a sensitive asset. Forward to SIEM. Once the stream exists, build per-actor anomaly detection (asset access at unusual hours, asset access from new IPs, asset access volume above the per-actor 95th percentile).
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1685`

- **SQL injection attempt against GET /orders** _(logsource=webserver, level=high)_ — Sigma id `f524ebfe-6d3a-50a4-839a-abd3906d532e`
- **Object access through POST /import** _(logsource=webserver, level=low + correlation)_ — Sigma id `d6ef4438-d989-5a7e-8b4f-9f54309e04a1`

detection_opportunities.title: Alert on unauthenticated access to sensitive-asset routes
detection_opportunities.rationale: A static-analysis gap on auth at the surface is also a runtime detection opportunity: any 2xx response for these routes from a request lacking a valid session/JWT is high signal.
detection_opportunities.suggested_rule: On the access log: alert when status_code IN (200,201,204) AND route IN (`/import`, `/signup`, `/orders`) AND request_headers.authorization IS NULL AND session_cookie IS NULL. Tighten with a low-volume baseline — this should normally be zero.

detection_opportunities.title: Add config-drift detection for missing controls on critical assets
detection_opportunities.rationale: When critical assets exist but expected controls aren't observable, drift detection on the deployed configuration (WAF rules, IAM policies, encryption-at-rest flags) gives ongoing visibility even before code-level fixes land.
detection_opportunities.suggested_rule: Add a daily IaC/config audit step: assert that the modules holding critical assets have (a) a WAF/auth policy attached, (b) database encryption-at-rest enabled, (c) audit-log subscriptions configured. Page when any assertion regresses.

detection_opportunities.rationale: Static analysis can't tell whether a control is invoked at runtime. Trace spans on the entry and sink confirm whether intermediate auth/validation/rate-limit middleware actually executed.

detection_opportunities.title: Establish baseline audit logs on sensitive-asset access
detection_opportunities.rationale: Detection is only as good as the telemetry available. The lack of audit-logging signals in code is a precondition: there is nothing for a SIEM to reason over.
detection_opportunities.suggested_rule: Emit a structured audit record `{actor, action, asset_id, outcome, request_id}` from every handler that touches a sensitive asset. Forward to SIEM. Once the stream exists, build per-actor anomaly detection (asset access at unusual hours, asset access from new IPs, asset access volume above the per-actor 95th percentile).
